correctness.rationale: The proof identifies the precise perturbed adjacency operator H^T H+ef^T+fe^T and a surjective (n+1)-dimensional incidence-coordinate quotient. The original H^T H has square zero in even n and is idempotent in odd n. The new coordinate map gives order four on im(A) for odd n, with fixed-space dimensions n-3 and n-1, and gives a swap on an exact two-dimensional recurrent image for even n. Explicit second-power ranks 2 (n=4) and 4 (even n>=6) establish sharp entrance bounds. Rank-nullity gives exact first-entrance and orbit basin populations, and subtraction of fixed-power populations gives primitive counts. All assertions are over arbitrary finite fields of characteristic two, and all necessary boundary cases are proved. Independent algorithms actually passed rank/iterate checks for n=4..16, exhaustive binary dynamical checks for n=4,5,6, and all GF(4) states for n=4.

originality.rationale: The claimed novelty is the complete period and basin classification after inserting one missing edge between disjoint two-subsets in J(n,2), including the parity change from nilpotence or idempotence to genuine primitive period two or four. Peeters gives unperturbed Johnson ranks and minimal polynomials; Ciandrini et al. give general XOR dynamical theory; exact published published-finding corpus work on even-even Johnson graphs instead removes an existing adjacency edge and produces six-periodic dynamics; and the Kneser-graph result acts on all complement edges rather than this single added one. Inspected material does not imply these new perturbed ranks or period counts. This does not establish universal priority against inaccessible or unindexed algebraic equivalents.
residual_risks: A general matrix rank-two graph-perturbation theorem outside indexed search may have this special case as an unadvertised corollary.
Some relevant historical full texts have not been inspected; a positive historical-priority certification is not possible.
The n=4 boundary belongs to a known complete-graph matching-deletion geometry; novelty rests on the infinite higher-order family and parity transition.

The 1994 preprint of Peeters is catalogued without a verified public day; 2008-09-09 denotes the first day-verified public source used to anchor the dynamics, not the first discovery of incidence rank results.

value.rationale: For the natural triangular Johnson graph, all previously missing edges form a single transitive orbit, so the edit is canonical and motivated. Its insertion changes the type of every recurrent attractor: nilpotent even graphs acquire two-cycles, idempotent odd graphs acquire four-cycles. The exact all-size complete orbit and basin populations and sharp n=4 versus n>=6 settling boundary quantify a genuine graph-sensitivity of the discrete dynamical system rather than a renamed classical rank identity or an arbitrary finite sample. The same proof works over all finite characteristic-two fields.
